Anatomy-03.question: ১) Accessory pancreatic duct is also called :
Anatomy-03.exp:
The accessory pancreatic duct is called the duct of Santorini. It drains a part of the pancreatic head and usually opens into the minor duodenal papilla.

The main pancreatic duct is called the duct of Wirsung, which drains most of the pancreas and opens into the major duodenal papilla along with the common bile duct.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Wirsung duct
    Main pancreatic duct, not the accessory duct.

  • খ) Santorini duct
    Accessory pancreatic duct.

  • গ) Henson's duct
    Not related to pancreatic drainage.

  • ঘ) Hoffman's duct
    Not a pancreatic duct.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Main pancreatic duct → Duct of Wirsung → Major duodenal papilla

  • Accessory pancreatic duct → Duct of Santorini → Minor duodenal papilla

  • Pancreas develops from dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds

Anatomy-03.question: ২) Which one is site of phonation?
৩) Respiratory zone excludes
৪) Payers patches are predominantly found in
৫) Uterine artery is a branch of which artery?
Anatomy-03.exp:
The uterine artery is a branch of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery. It supplies the uterus and also gives branches to the cervix, vagina, and uterine tubes.

A key anatomical relationship:

  • Ureter passes under the uterine artery

  • Remember: “Water under the bridge”

    • Water = ureter

    • Bridge = uterine artery

Option Analysis

  • ক) External iliac
    Gives branches mainly supplying the lower limb; not the uterine artery.

  • খ) Internal iliac
    Gives the uterine artery through its anterior division.

  • গ) Pudendal
    Supplies perineum and external genital structures.

  • ঘ) Femoral
    Supplies the lower limb.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Uterine artery → Internal iliac artery

  • Ovarian artery → Abdominal aorta

  • Uterine artery crosses over ureter → “Water under the bridge”

Anatomy-03.question: ৬) Somatostatin is secreted from which cell?
৭) Serous demilune are present in
৮) “supplies oxygenated blood to hepatocyte”-
৯) Centroacinar cells are present in
১০) Blood supply of liver is :
Anatomy-03.exp:
The liver has a dual blood supply:

  • Portal vein: Provides about 75–80% of hepatic blood flow and supplies nutrient-rich blood from the gastrointestinal tract and spleen.

  • Hepatic artery: Provides about 20–25% of hepatic blood flow and supplies oxygenated arterial blood.

Although the hepatic artery contributes less blood flow, it provides a significant amount of oxygen because arterial blood has a higher oxygen content.

Option Analysis

  • ক) 80% arterial, 20% venous
    Incorrect; the majority of blood flow is from the portal vein.

  • খ) 70% arterial, 30% venous
    Incorrect; arterial contribution is overestimated.

  • গ) 80% venous, 20% arterial
    Correct; portal venous supply provides the majority of hepatic blood flow.

  • ঘ) 60% arterial, 40% venous
    Incorrect; does not represent normal hepatic circulation.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Liver blood supply: Portal vein ~75–80%, Hepatic artery ~20–25%

  • Portal vein → Nutrients + majority of blood flow

  • Hepatic artery → Oxygen supply

  • Bile flows opposite to blood: Hepatocyte → bile canaliculi → ducts

Anatomy-03.question: ১১) Pain of gallstones is referred to following areas except :
Anatomy-03.exp:
Pain from gallstones (biliary colic) is typically referred to the right shoulder tip due to irritation of the diaphragm and involvement of the phrenic nerve (C3–C5). It may also be felt in the epigastrium.

The classic referred pain sites include:

  • Right shoulder tip

  • Right scapular region (especially inferior angle of right scapula)

  • Epigastrium

The inferior angle of the left scapula is not a typical site of gallstone pain referral.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Tip of right shoulder
    Common referred pain site due to diaphragmatic irritation.

  • খ) Epigastric region
    Common site of visceral pain from gallbladder.

  • গ) Inferior angle of left scapula
    Not a typical referred pain site for gallstones.

  • ঘ) Right shoulder
    Common referred pain site.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Gallstone pain → Right shoulder tip + right scapular region + epigastrium

  • Referred shoulder pain → Phrenic nerve (C3, C4, C5)

  • Gallbladder visceral afferents → T7–T9 spinal segm

Anatomy-03.question: ১২) Cancer from the testis would most likely metastasize first to the :
Anatomy-03.exp:
The testis drains lymphatically to the para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes because it develops embryologically in the posterior abdominal wall and descends into the scrotum.

Therefore, testicular carcinoma most commonly metastasizes first to the lumbar (para-aortic) lymph nodes.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Lumbar nodes
    First site of lymphatic spread from testicular cancer.

  • খ) Superficial inguinal nodes
    Drain the skin of the scrotum, not the testis itself.

  • গ) Deep inguinal nodes
    Drain structures of the lower limb and external genital region, not the primary lymphatic drainage of the testis.

  • ঘ) Internal iliac nodes
    Receive lymph from pelvic organs but are not the first drainage site of the testis.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Testis → Para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes

  • Scrotal skin → Superficial inguinal lymph nodes

  • Testis and ovary share similar lymphatic drainage → Para-aortic nodes

  • Testis descends from abdomen → retains abdominal lymphatic draina

Anatomy-03.question: ১৩) The esophageal hiatus transmits the esophagus & the :
Anatomy-03.exp:
(Ref: medical examination review anatomy P:53)

The esophageal hiatus of the diaphragm (at the level of T10 vertebra) transmits:

  • Esophagus

  • Anterior and posterior vagal trunks

The vagal trunks accompany the esophagus through the diaphragm and contribute to the autonomic supply of the abdominal gastrointestinal tract.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Superior phrenic artery
    Passes through the diaphragm but not through the esophageal hiatus.

  • খ) Thoracic duct
    Passes through the aortic hiatus (T12).

  • গ) Vagal nerve trunk
    Transmitted through the esophageal hiatus along with the esophagus.

  • ঘ) Greater splanchnic nerve
    Pierces the crura of the diaphragm separately, not through the esophageal hiatus.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • T8 → Caval opening → Inferior vena cava

  • T10 → Esophageal hiatus → Esophagus + vagal trunks

  • T12 → Aortic hiatus → Aorta + thoracic duct

Anatomy-03.question: ১৪) Principal artery of Rectum—
Anatomy-03.exp:
The superior rectal artery is the principal artery supplying the rectum. It is the continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery and supplies the upper part of the rectum.

Other arterial supplies:

  • Middle rectal artery → branch of internal iliac artery; supplies lower rectum

  • Inferior rectal artery → branch of internal pudendal artery; supplies anal canal

  • Median sacral artery → minor contribution

Option Analysis

  • ক) Superior rectal artery
    Principal arterial supply of the rectum.

  • খ) Middle rectal artery
    Provides additional supply to the rectum.

  • গ) Median sacral artery
    Supplies posterior pelvic structures; minor rectal contribution.

  • ঘ) Inferior rectal artery
    Supplies lower anal canal and surrounding structures.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Rectum principal artery → Superior rectal artery

  • Superior rectal artery → Inferior mesenteric artery

  • Middle rectal artery → Internal iliac artery

  • Inferior rectal artery → Internal pudendal artery

  • Anal canal below pectinate line → Inferior rectal artery

Anatomy-03.question: ১৫) Most dependent part of abdomen in lying position -
Anatomy-03.exp:
In the supine (lying) position, the most dependent part of the peritoneal cavity is the hepato-renal pouch (Morison’s pouch), which is the space between the right lobe of the liver and the right kidney.

It is an important site for accumulation of:

  • Free intraperitoneal fluid

  • Blood after trauma

  • Pus in peritonitis

Option Analysis

  • ক) Pelvic cavity
    The pelvic cavity is the most dependent part in the standing position.

  • খ) Iliac fossa
    Not the most dependent part in the supine position.

  • গ) Hepato-renal pouch
    Most dependent part of the peritoneal cavity when lying supine.

  • ঘ) Greater sac
    A large peritoneal compartment but not the most dependent area.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Supine position → Hepato-renal pouch (Morison’s pouch)

  • Standing position → Pelvic cavity (rectovesical pouch/rectouterine pouch)

  • Morison’s pouch → Common site for intraperitoneal fluid collection

Anatomy-03.question: ১৬) True ligament of liver—
Anatomy-03.exp:
The true ligaments of the liver are peritoneal folds that attach the liver to surrounding structures. The falciform ligament is considered a true ligament of the liver and attaches the liver to the anterior abdominal wall and diaphragm.

Other true ligaments include:

  • Coronary ligament

  • Triangular ligaments

Option Analysis

  • ক) Falciform ligament
    A true peritoneal ligament of the liver.

  • খ) Coronary ligament
    Also a true ligament of the liver, but the best single answer in this list is falciform ligament.

  • গ) Ligamentum venosum
    A fibrous remnant of the ductus venosus; not a true peritoneal ligament.

  • ঘ) Lesser omentum
    A peritoneal fold connecting liver with stomach and duodenum; not classified as a true ligament.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • True ligaments of liver → Falciform, coronary, triangular ligaments

  • Ligamentum teres hepatis → Remnant of umbilical vein

  • Ligamentum venosum → Remnant of ductus venosus

  • Lesser omentum → Hepatogastric + hepatoduodenal ligaments

Anatomy-03.question: ১৭) Main support of liver -
Anatomy-03.exp:
The hepatic veins are considered an important main support of the liver, as they anchor the liver to the inferior vena cava and posterior abdominal wall. The liver is also supported by its peritoneal ligaments, especially the falciform and coronary ligaments, but these are not the principal mechanical support. The hepatic veins pass from the liver directly into the inferior vena cava, helping maintain the liver's position. Therefore, among the given options, hepatic vein is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Main support of liver → Hepatic veins
Hepatic veins → Drain into IVC
Falciform ligament → Divides anatomical right and left lobes
Coronary ligament → Helps attach liver to diaphragm
Liver is largely intraperitoneal except for the bare area
Exam Pearl: Hepatic veins are the major posterior anchoring support of the liver.

Anatomy-03.question: ১৮) Main branches of celiac trunk excludes
Anatomy-03.exp:
The celiac trunk is the first major branch of the abdominal aorta and gives three main branches:

  • Left gastric artery

  • Splenic artery

  • Common hepatic artery

The pancreatic arteries are branches of the splenic artery or gastroduodenal artery, not direct branches of the celiac trunk.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Left gastric artery
    One of the three main branches of the celiac trunk.

  • খ) Splenic artery
    One of the three main branches of the celiac trunk.

  • গ) Common hepatic artery
    One of the three main branches of the celiac trunk.

  • ঘ) Pancreatic artery
    Not a direct branch of the celiac trunk.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Celiac trunk branches → Left gastric + Splenic + Common hepatic

  • Mnemonic: LSC (Left gastric, Splenic, Common hepatic)

  • Splenic artery gives pancreatic branches

  • Gastroduodenal artery gives pancreaticoduodenal branches

Anatomy-03.question: ১৯) The posterior boundary of epiploic foramen is formed by the :
Anatomy-03.exp:
The epiploic foramen (omental foramen of Winslow) is the opening connecting the greater sac with the lesser sac.

Its boundaries are:

  • Anterior: Hepatoduodenal ligament (contains portal vein, hepatic artery, and bile duct)

  • Posterior: Inferior vena cava

  • Superior: Caudate lobe of liver

  • Inferior: First part of duodenum

Option Analysis

  • ক) Duodenum
    Forms the inferior boundary, not the posterior boundary.

  • খ) Lesser omentum
    Forms the anterior boundary through the hepatoduodenal ligament.

  • গ) Inferior vena cava
    Forms the posterior boundary of the epiploic foramen.

  • ঘ) Transverse colon
    Not a boundary of the epiploic foramen.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Epiploic foramen posterior boundary → Inferior vena cava

  • Anterior boundary → Hepatoduodenal ligament

  • Superior boundary → Caudate lobe of liver

  • Inferior boundary → First part of duodenum

Anatomy-03.question: ২০) The superior mesenteric artery supplies each of the following except the :
Anatomy-03.exp:
The superior mesenteric artery (SMA) supplies the midgut derivatives. It supplies structures from the distal duodenum to the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon.

Branches of SMA include:

  • Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery → pancreas and duodenum

  • Ileocolic artery → ileum, caecum, appendix

  • Middle colic artery → proximal two-thirds of transverse colon

The rectum is supplied mainly by the superior rectal artery (branch of inferior mesenteric artery) and middle/inferior rectal arteries.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Appendix
    Supplied by appendicular artery, a branch of ileocolic artery from SMA.

  • খ) Rectum
    Not supplied by SMA.

  • গ) Pancreas
    Supplied partly by inferior pancreaticoduodenal branches of SMA.

  • ঘ) Transverse colon
    Proximal two-thirds supplied by middle colic artery from SMA.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • SMA → Midgut supply

  • SMA supplies: distal duodenum, jejunum, ileum, caecum, appendix, ascending colon, proximal 2/3 transverse colon

  • IMA supplies: distal 1/3 transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon, upper rectum

  • Rectum → Mainly inferior mesenteric artery territory

Anatomy-03.question: ২১) Which of the following sites of primary cancer is most likely to give rise to metastases in the lung by venous spread?
Anatomy-03.exp:
The lung is a common site of metastasis through venous spread because venous blood from many organs enters the systemic circulation and passes through the pulmonary circulation.

Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) commonly spreads via the renal vein → inferior vena cava → right side of heart → pulmonary arteries → lungs, producing lung metastases.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Ileum
    Tumours usually spread via the portal circulation to the liver before reaching other sites.

  • খ) Appendix
    More commonly spreads within the peritoneal cavity or through lymphatics.

  • গ) Kidney
    Renal cell carcinoma has characteristic venous spread to the lungs.

  • ঘ) Transverse colon
    Colonic cancers mainly spread via portal venous drainage to the liver.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Kidney cancer → Renal vein → IVC → Lung metastasis

  • GI tract cancers → Portal vein → Liver metastasis

  • Lung is the commonest site of haematogenous metastasis

  • RCC is known for tumour thrombus formation in renal vein and IVC

Anatomy-03.question: ২২) The lateral boundary of the inguinal triangle is the :
Anatomy-03.exp:
The inguinal triangle (Hesselbach’s triangle) is the weak area of the anterior abdominal wall where direct inguinal hernias occur.

Its boundaries are:

  • Medial: Lateral border of rectus abdominis muscle

  • Lateral: Inferior epigastric vessels

  • Inferior: Inguinal ligament

Option Analysis

  • ক) Inguinal ligament
    Forms the inferior boundary of the inguinal triangle.

  • খ) Rectus abdominis muscle
    Forms the medial boundary.

  • গ) Urogenital diaphragm
    Not a boundary of the inguinal triangle.

  • ঘ) Inferior epigastric artery
    Forms the lateral boundary of Hesselbach’s triangle.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Hesselbach’s triangle boundaries:

    • Medial → Rectus abdominis

    • Lateral → Inferior epigastric vessels

    • Inferior → Inguinal ligament

  • Direct inguinal hernia → Medial to inferior epigastric vessels

  • Indirect inguinal hernia → Lateral to inferior epigastric vessels

Anatomy-03.question: ২৩) Each of the following arteries is a direct or indirect branch of the internal iliac artery except the :
Anatomy-03.exp:
The inferior epigastric artery is not a branch of the internal iliac artery. It arises from the external iliac artery just above the inguinal ligament.

The internal iliac artery supplies pelvic structures through its anterior and posterior divisions.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Obturator artery
    Usually a branch of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery.

  • খ) Artery of the ductus deferens
    A branch of the superior vesical artery, which arises from the internal iliac artery.

  • গ) Inferior epigastric artery
    Branch of the external iliac artery, not related to internal iliac artery.

  • ঘ) Middle rectal artery
    A branch of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Internal iliac branches → Obturator, middle rectal, superior vesical, uterine, vaginal, internal pudendal

  • Inferior epigastric artery → External iliac artery

  • Inferior epigastric vessels → Lateral boundary of Hesselbach’s triang

Anatomy-03.question: ২৪) Contents of spermatic cord excludes -
Anatomy-03.exp:
The ilioinguinal nerve does not pass within the spermatic cord. It travels through the inguinal canal and emerges through the superficial inguinal ring, but it lies outside the spermatic cord.

Contents of the spermatic cord include:

  • Vas deferens

  • Testicular artery

  • Pampiniform plexus (testicular veins)

  • Cremasteric artery

  • Artery of ductus deferens

  • Genital branch of genitofemoral nerve

  • Sympathetic nerve fibres

  • Lymphatics

Option Analysis

  • ক) Testicular vein
    Present as the pampiniform plexus within the spermatic cord.

  • খ) Ilioinguinal nerve
    Not a content of the spermatic cord.

  • গ) Cremasteric artery
    A content of the spermatic cord.

  • ঘ) Plexus of sympathetic nerves
    Present along the vas deferens and testicular vessels.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Spermatic cord → Vas deferens + testicular vessels + nerves + lymphatics

  • Genital branch of genitofemoral nerve → Inside spermatic cord

  • Ilioinguinal nerve → Travels in inguinal canal but outside spermatic cord

  • Pampiniform plexus → Testicular veins

Anatomy-03.question: ২৫) Retroperitoneal organs exclude-
Anatomy-03.exp:
The retroperitoneal organs are structures located behind the parietal peritoneum. The spleen is an intraperitoneal organ, not retroperitoneal.

Important retroperitoneal organs include:

  • Kidneys

  • Suprarenal glands

  • Ureters

  • Abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava

  • Most of the pancreas (except tail)

  • Second to fourth parts of duodenum

  • Ascending and descending colon

Option Analysis

  • ক) Spleen
    Intraperitoneal organ; not retroperitoneal.

  • খ) Pancreas
    Mostly retroperitoneal except the tail.

  • গ) Aorta
    Located in the retroperitoneum.

  • ঘ) Kidney
    Classic retroperitoneal organ.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Retroperitoneal mnemonic: SAD PUCKER

    • Suprarenal glands

    • Aorta/IVC

    • Duodenum (2nd–4th parts)

    • Pancreas (except tail)

    • Ureters

    • Colon (ascending & descending)

    • Kidneys

    • Esophagus

    • Rectum

  • Spleen → Intraperitoneal

  • Kidney → Retroperitoneal

Anatomy-03.question: ২৬) Abdominal aorta begins at the level of
Anatomy-03.exp:
The abdominal aorta begins at the level of T12 vertebra after passing through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm.

It continues downward and ends at the level of L4 vertebra by dividing into the two common iliac arteries.

Option Analysis

  • ক) T11
    Not the level of aortic entry into the abdomen.

  • খ) T12
    Level of the aortic hiatus and beginning of the abdominal aorta.

  • গ) L4
    Level of bifurcation of the abdominal aorta into common iliac arteries.

  • ঘ) L5
    Not a major landmark for the abdominal aorta.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Aortic hiatus → T12 → Abdominal aorta begins

  • Caval opening → T8 → Inferior vena cava

  • Oesophageal hiatus → T10 → Oesophagus + vagal trunks

  • Aortic bifurcation → L4

Anatomy-03.question: ২৭) Continuation of abdominal aorta
Anatomy-03.exp:
The abdominal aorta terminates at the level of L4 vertebra by dividing into the right and left common iliac arteries.

The common iliac arteries then divide into:

  • Internal iliac artery → supplies pelvic organs

  • External iliac artery → continues as femoral artery to supply lower limb

Option Analysis

  • ক) Common iliac artery
    Terminal continuation of the abdominal aorta.

  • খ) Median sacral artery
    A small midline branch arising from the posterior aspect of the abdominal aorta near its bifurcation.

  • গ) Internal iliac artery
    A branch of the common iliac artery.

  • ঘ) External iliac artery
    A branch of the common iliac artery.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Abdominal aorta begins → T12

  • Abdominal aorta ends → L4

  • Termination → Right and left common iliac arteries

  • Common iliac → Internal iliac + External iliac

Anatomy-03.question: ২৮) Main artery of stomach
Anatomy-03.exp:
The left gastric artery is considered the main artery of the stomach. It is the largest and most important branch of the celiac trunk and supplies the upper part of the stomach, especially the lesser curvature.

The stomach has a rich arterial supply through anastomoses:

  • Left gastric artery → lesser curvature

  • Right gastric artery → lesser curvature

  • Left gastro-epiploic artery → greater curvature

  • Right gastro-epiploic artery → greater curvature

  • Short gastric arteries → fundus

Option Analysis

  • ক) Right gastric artery
    Supplies the lesser curvature but is smaller than the left gastric artery.

  • খ) Left gastric artery
    Main artery of the stomach and direct branch of the celiac trunk.

  • গ) Left gastro-epiploic artery
    Supplies the greater curvature; branch of splenic artery.

  • ঘ) Splenic artery
    Supplies the stomach through its branches but is not the main gastric artery.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Main artery of stomach → Left gastric artery

  • Left gastric artery → Celiac trunk

  • Splenic artery → Left gastro-epiploic + short gastric arteries

  • Gastric arteries run along lesser and greater curvatur

Anatomy-03.question: ২৯) Most dilated part of GIT—
Anatomy-03.exp:
The stomach is the most dilated part of the gastrointestinal tract (GIT). It acts as a reservoir for food and can accommodate a large volume due to its expandable muscular wall.

The stomach has four main regions:

  • Cardia

  • Fundus

  • Body

  • Pylorus

Option Analysis

  • ক) Stomach
    Most dilated part of the GIT.

  • খ) Rectum
    Can distend to store faeces but is not the most dilated part of GIT.

  • গ) Sigmoid colon
    A reservoir-like part of the large intestine but not the most dilated.

  • ঘ) Anus
    Terminal part of GIT; not dilated.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Most dilated part of GIT → Stomach

  • Longest part of GIT → Small intestine

  • Largest digestive gland → Liver

  • Longest organ of GIT → Small intestine

Anatomy-03.question: ৩০) Appendicular artery is a branch of
Anatomy-03.exp:
The appendicular artery is a branch of the ileocolic artery, which arises from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). It runs within the mesoappendix to supply the appendix.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Right colic artery
    Supplies the ascending colon; does not give the appendicular artery.

  • খ) Middle colic artery
    Supplies the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon.

  • গ) Left colic artery
    Branch of inferior mesenteric artery; supplies the descending colon.

  • ঘ) Ileocolic artery
    Gives the appendicular artery and supplies the appendix.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Appendix blood supply → Appendicular artery

  • Appendicular artery → Ileocolic artery → Superior mesenteric artery

  • Appendix lymph drainage → Ileocolic lymph nodes

  • Appendix pain → Initially periumbilical (T10), later right iliac fossa

Anatomy-03.question: ৩১) Most common position of appendix -
Anatomy-03.exp:
The most common position of the appendix is retro-cecal, where the appendix lies behind the caecum. It accounts for approximately 60–65% of cases.

Other positions include:

  • Pelvic

  • Sub-cecal

  • Pre-ileal

  • Post-ileal

Option Analysis

  • ক) Preileal
    Less common position; appendix lies anterior to the ileum.

  • খ) Postileal
    Less common position; appendix lies posterior to the ileum.

  • গ) Retro-cecal
    Most common position of the appendix.

  • ঘ) Sub-cecal
    Less common position; appendix lies below the caecum.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Most common appendix position → Retro-cecal

  • Appendix base → Convergence of three taeniae coli

  • Appendix artery → Appendicular artery (branch of ileocolic artery)

  • McBurney’s point → Surface marking of appendix base

Anatomy-03.question: ৩২) Stomach bed excludes-
Anatomy-03.exp:
The stomach bed refers to the structures lying posterior to the stomach that support it. Important components include:

  • Diaphragm

  • Spleen

  • Left kidney

  • Left suprarenal gland

  • Pancreas

  • Splenic artery and vein

  • Transverse mesocolon

  • Left colic flexure (sometimes included as a related structure)

However, in standard anatomical descriptions, the left colic flexure is not considered a major component of the stomach bed.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Spleen
    A major structure in the stomach bed.

  • খ) Splenic vein
    Lies posterior to the stomach as part of the pancreaticosplenic region.

  • গ) Left colic flexure
    Not considered a principal structure of the stomach bed.

  • ঘ) Left kidney
    A major posterior relation of the stomach.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Stomach bed → Diaphragm, spleen, left kidney, pancreas, splenic vessels, left suprarenal gland

  • Posterior relation of stomach → Pancreas is an important surgical landmark

  • Lesser sac lies behind the stomach

Anatomy-03.question: ৩৩) Derivatives of dorsal mesogastrium-
Anatomy-03.exp:
The dorsal mesogastrium is an embryological peritoneal fold attached to the posterior aspect of the stomach. It gives rise mainly to the greater omentum and related structures.

During development:

  • The dorsal mesogastrium enlarges and forms the greater omentum.

  • It also contributes to structures related to the spleen and lesser sac formation.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Greater omentum
    Derived from the dorsal mesogastrium.

  • খ) Lesser omentum
    Derived from the ventral mesogastrium.

  • গ) Falciform ligament
    Derived from the ventral mesogastrium.

  • ঘ) Coronary ligament
    Derived from the ventral mesogastrium.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Dorsal mesogastrium → Greater omentum + splenic ligaments

  • Ventral mesogastrium → Lesser omentum + falciform ligament

  • Falciform ligament contains ligamentum teres hepatis (obliterated umbilical vein)

Anatomy-03.question: ৩৪) Regarding descent of the testes, which one is not true?
Anatomy-03.option2: 4th month-rest on the deep inguinal ring
Anatomy-03.exp:
The descent of the testes occurs in two phases:

  • Transabdominal phase: Testis descends from the posterior abdominal wall to the deep inguinal ring during early fetal life.

  • Inguinoscrotal phase: Testis passes through the inguinal canal and reaches the scrotum mainly during the 7th month onwards.

Therefore, saying that the testes traverse the inguinal canal in the 5th month is incorrect.

Option Analysis

  • ক) 2nd month – begins to descend
    Generally considered correct; testicular descent begins early in fetal life.

  • খ) 4th month – rests on the deep inguinal ring
    Correct; the testis reaches the region of the deep inguinal ring.

  • গ) 5th month – traverse the inguinal canal
    Incorrect; passage through the inguinal canal occurs later, mainly around the 7th month.

  • ঘ) 9th month – bottom of scrotum
    Correct; testes usually reach the scrotum before birth.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Testis descent begins → 2nd month

  • Reaches deep inguinal ring → 4th month

  • Passes inguinal canal → ~7th month

  • Reaches scrotum → Before birth (9th month)

  • Gubernaculum guides testicular descent

Anatomy-03.question: ৩৫) Regarding development of pancreas-
Anatomy-03.option1: It originates at 4th week of gestation as paired evaginations of the foregut
Anatomy-03.option2: The ventral bud gives rise to body and tail
Anatomy-03.option3: In 50% of cases the duct system fail to fuse
Anatomy-03.option4: The dorsal bud gives rise to uncinate process.
Anatomy-03.exp:
The pancreas develops from two endodermal buds arising from the foregut:

  • Dorsal pancreatic bud

  • Ventral pancreatic bud

The two buds normally fuse during development, including their duct systems. Failure of duct fusion occurs in approximately 10% of cases, resulting in pancreas divisum, not 50%.

Option Analysis

  • ক) It originates at 4th week of gestation as paired evaginations of the foregut
    Correct. Pancreas develops from dorsal and ventral endodermal buds around the 4th week.

  • খ) The ventral bud gives rise to body and tail
    Incorrect. The ventral bud forms the uncinate process and inferior part of the head.

  • গ) In 50% of cases the duct system fail to fuse
    Incorrect. Duct fusion failure occurs in about 10% of individuals.

  • ঘ) The dorsal bud gives rise to uncinate process
    Incorrect. The dorsal bud forms the body, tail, and superior part of the head.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Dorsal pancreatic bud → Body, tail, and upper head

  • Ventral pancreatic bud → Uncinate process and lower head

  • Failure of duct fusion → Pancreas divisum (~10%)

  • Main pancreatic duct → Formed by fusion of dorsal and ventral ducts

Anatomy-03.question: ৩৬) Urethra passes through which part of penis?
৩৭) Homologus structure of penis in female
৩৮) The classic hepatic lobule emphasizes
Anatomy-03.exp:
The classic hepatic lobule is the structural unit of the liver that emphasizes the exocrine function of hepatocytes, i.e., bile secretion.

In the classic hepatic lobule:

  • Hepatocytes are arranged in plates around a central vein

  • Bile flows from hepatocytes through bile canaliculi toward the portal triads

  • Blood flows in the opposite direction from portal triads toward the central vein

Option Analysis

  • ক) Endocrine function of hepatocyte
    Not emphasized by the classic hepatic lobule.

  • খ) Exocrine function of hepatocyte
    Correct; classic lobule is based on bile drainage.

  • গ) Oxygen content of blood
    Emphasized by the hepatic acinus, not the classic lobule.

  • ঘ) Nutrient content of blood
    Also related to the hepatic acinus concept.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Classic hepatic lobule → Bile secretion (exocrine function)

  • Portal lobule → Bile drainage

  • Hepatic acinus → Blood flow, oxygen and nutrient gradient

  • Zone 1 (acinus) → Highest oxygen

  • Zone 3 → Most vulnerable to ischaemia and toxins

Anatomy-03.question: ৩৯) Oesophagus ends at -
৪০) Innermost muscular layer of stomach
৪১) Inferior venacava passes through—
Anatomy-03.exp:
The inferior vena cava (IVC) passes through the caval opening of the diaphragm, which is located at the level of T8 vertebra.

The caval opening is situated in the central tendon of the diaphragm, making it a tendinous opening.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Muscular opening
    Incorrect. The aortic hiatus is not muscular either; it lies posterior to the diaphragm.

  • খ) Tendinous opening
    Correct. The IVC passes through the central tendon of the diaphragm.

  • গ) Aponeurotic opening
    Not the standard anatomical description of the caval opening.

  • ঘ) Osseoaponeurotic opening
    Not related to the IVC passage.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • T8 → Caval opening → Inferior vena cava → Central tendon

  • T10 → Oesophageal hiatus → Oesophagus + vagal trunks → Muscular part

  • T12 → Aortic hiatus → Aorta + thoracic duct → Behind diaphragm

Anatomy-03.question: ৪২) Anterior relation of right kidney-
Anatomy-03.exp:
The right kidney has the following important anterior relations:

  • Right suprarenal gland

  • Liver

  • Second part of duodenum

  • Hepatic flexure of colon

  • Small intestine

The spleen and stomach are related to the left kidney, while the pancreas is mainly related to the left kidney anteriorly.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Right suprarenal gland
    Anterior relation of the right kidney.

  • খ) Spleen
    Anterior relation of the left kidney.

  • গ) Pancreas
    Mainly related to the left kidney anteriorly.

  • ঘ) Stomach
    Related to the left kidney, not the right.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Right kidney anterior relations → Liver, right suprarenal gland, duodenum, hepatic flexure

  • Left kidney anterior relations → Stomach, spleen, pancreas, jejunum, splenic flexure

  • Kidneys are retroperitoneal organs

Anatomy-03.question: ৪৩) Structures developing from the dorsal mesentery-
Anatomy-03.exp:
The dorsal mesentery is an embryological peritoneal fold attached to the posterior aspect of the primitive gut. It gives rise to several structures, including the greater omentum.

The dorsal mesentery derivatives include:

  • Greater omentum

  • Mesentery of small intestine

  • Transverse mesocolon

  • Sigmoid mesocolon

  • Mesoappendix

  • Splenic ligaments (including lienorenal ligament)

Option Analysis

  • ক) Mesoappendix
    Derived from the dorsal mesentery.

  • খ) Greater omentum
    A major derivative of the dorsal mesentery.

  • গ) Lienorenal ligament
    Derived from the dorsal mesogastrium (part of dorsal mesentery).

  • ঘ) Lesser omentum
    Derived from the ventral mesentery, not dorsal.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Dorsal mesentery → Greater omentum, mesentery, mesocolons, mesoappendix, splenic ligaments

  • Ventral mesentery → Lesser omentum + falciform ligament

  • Dorsal mesogastrium → Greater omentum + gastrosplenic/lienorenal ligaments

Anatomy-03.question: ৪৪) The pleura is a serous membrane which is lined by -
Anatomy-03.exp:
The pleura is a serous membrane lined by simple squamous epithelium, which is specifically called mesothelium.

The mesothelium:

  • Provides a smooth, frictionless surface

  • Secretes serous fluid that allows movement of the lungs during respiration

Option Analysis

  • ক) Simple squamous epithelium
    Correct. Serous membranes including pleura are lined by mesothelium (simple squamous epithelium).

  • খ) Simple cuboidal epithelium
    Not the lining of pleura.

  • গ) Simple columnar epithelium
    Found in structures such as parts of the gastrointestinal tract, not pleura.

  • ঘ) None of above
    Incorrect because pleura is lined by simple squamous epithelium.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Pleura → Mesothelium → Simple squamous epithelium

  • Serous membranes: Pleura, pericardium, peritoneum

  • Mesothelium produces serous fluid for friction-free movement

Anatomy-03.question: ৪৫) Secretion in what neuroendocrine cell is controlled directly by neural activity and involves a hormone that generally slows metabolic activity at night?
Anatomy-03.exp:
Pinealocytes are neuroendocrine cells of the pineal gland that secrete melatonin. Their secretion is directly controlled by neural activity from the sympathetic nervous system.

Melatonin secretion:

  • Increases during darkness/night

  • Helps regulate the sleep–wake cycle

  • Generally decreases metabolic activity and promotes rest during nighttime

Option Analysis

  • ক) Pituicyte
    Supporting cells of the posterior pituitary; involved with storage and release of ADH and oxytocin from hypothalamic neurons.

  • খ) Melanocyte
    Produces melanin pigment; not a neuroendocrine cell involved in circadian regulation.

  • গ) Chromaffin cell
    Neuroendocrine cells of adrenal medulla that secrete catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline).

  • ঘ) Pinealocyte
    Produces melatonin under neural control.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Pinealocyte → Melatonin → Circadian rhythm

  • Melatonin secretion ↑ in darkness

  • Pineal gland = biological clock

  • Chromaffin cells → Catecholamines

  • Pituicytes → Posterior pituitary support

Anatomy-03.question: ৪৬) Which hormone suppresses immune cell activities?
৪৭) Secretion, chemical modification and storage, reuptake, and digestion of a protein occur in epithelial cells of what endocrine tissue?
Anatomy-03.exp:
The adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) contains endocrine epithelial cells that synthesize, chemically modify, store, and secrete protein hormones.

Examples of protein hormones produced by adenohypophyseal cells:

  • Growth hormone (GH)

  • Prolactin (PRL)

  • ACTH

  • TSH

  • FSH and LH

These hormones are synthesized as proteins, processed within the cells, stored in secretory granules, and released by exocytosis.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Neurohypophysis
    Stores and releases ADH and oxytocin, which are synthesized by hypothalamic neurons; it does not synthesize these proteins.

  • খ) Adrenal medulla
    Contains chromaffin cells that secrete catecholamines, which are derived from amino acids, not protein hormones.

  • গ) Adenohypophysis
    Contains epithelial endocrine cells responsible for synthesis, processing, storage, and secretion of protein hormones.

  • ঘ) Thyroid gland
    Synthesizes thyroid hormones from thyroglobulin, but the described protein hormone secretion process is characteristic of anterior pituitary cells.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Adenohypophysis → Epithelial endocrine cells → Protein hormones

  • Neurohypophysis → Stores/releases ADH and oxytocin from hypothalamus

  • Adrenal medulla → Catecholamines (tyrosine-derived)

  • Thyroid → T3/T4 synthesis from iodinated thyroglobulin

Anatomy-03.question: ৪৮) Which bone accommodates pituitary gland?
৪৯) Chromaffin cells are present in
Anatomy-03.exp:
Chromaffin cells are specialized neuroendocrine cells located in the adrenal medulla. They are derived from neural crest cells and function like modified sympathetic postganglionic neurons.

They secrete:

  • Adrenaline (epinephrine)

  • Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)

in response to sympathetic stimulation.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Adrenal medulla
    Correct. Contains chromaffin cells that release catecholamines.

  • খ) Adrenal cortex
    Produces steroid hormones: glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, and androgens.

  • গ) Parathyroid gland
    Contains chief cells and oxyphil cells; secretes parathyroid hormone.

  • ঘ) Neurohypophysis
    Stores and releases ADH and oxytocin produced by hypothalamic neurons.

High-Yield / Rapid Recall

  • Chromaffin cells → Adrenal medulla → Catecholamines

  • Adrenal cortex → GFR hormones

    • Glucocorticoids

    • Mineralocorticoids

    • Androgens

  • Chromaffin cells are modified sympathetic postganglionic neurons
